matches.text: Loss curves can oscillate or rise for several reasons. Reducing a learning rate can be useful when debugging an oscillating training-loss curve. When training loss improves but validation loss rises, overfitting is one possible interpretation. These are general diagnostic ideas, not proof of a cause for any particular saved run.

matches.source_title: Validation curves: plotting scores to evaluate models
matches.text: Training and validation scores together can help identify possible overfitting. A high training score paired with a lower validation score is a warning that performance may not generalize as well to unseen data. A pattern in one short saved curve is only a candidate signal; other explanations and repeated checks remain possible.
